Ministry of Textiles Organized Workshops on Cyber Security & Secure Digital Disposal and E-Waste Management Awareness under Special Campaign 6
articles.full_content:
As part of Special Campaign 6, the Ministry of Textiles organised workshops on E-Waste Management Awareness and Cyber Security & Secure Digital Disposal on 15 October 2026, with the participation of over 85 officials, including all Nodal Officers. The workshops aimed to promote responsible e-waste management, strengthen cyber security awareness and encourage safe digital practices in the workplace.
A dedicated Cyber Security Awareness Session was organised to familiarise officials and staff with emerging cyber threats, including phishing attacks, malware, fraudulent WhatsApp messages and digital arrest scams. The session highlighted the importance of identifying suspicious emails, links, attachments and messages, particularly those impersonating known contacts or seeking money, one-time passwords (OTPs) or personal information.
Participants were advised to exercise caution while handling digital communications, refrain from clicking on unknown links or downloading unverified files, avoid sharing sensitive information, and verify the authenticity of suspicious communications before taking any action. The session also emphasised the importance of cyber hygiene, vigilance and the timely reporting of cyber incidents to safeguard official and personal information.
The E-Waste Management Awareness session sensitised officials to the adverse environmental impact of improper e-waste disposal, including soil and water contamination and the release of hazardous substances that may pose risks to human health and ecosystems. They highlighted the importance of resource conservation through the reuse, refurbishment and recycling of electronic equipment, wherever feasible, to recover valuable materials, reduce the demand for raw materials and minimise the volume of waste sent to landfills. Officials were also made aware of the need for proper segregation, safe handling and disposal of obsolete electronic and electrical equipment through authorised channels, in accordance with applicable e-waste management rules.
The sessions encouraged the adoption of sustainable office practices, emphasising that responsible e-waste management contributes to environmental protection, efficient resource utilisation and the promotion of a circular economy.
These initiatives reflect the Ministry of Textiles’ commitment to promoting a cleaner workplace, ensuring responsible resource management and fostering a secure digital environment. By integrating environmental sustainability with cyber security awareness, the Ministry continues to advance the objectives of Special Campaign 6 through improved workplace practices, resource conservation and enhanced digital safety.
The Ministry has also undertaken initiatives for the collection and proper management of e-waste generated within its premises, emphasising the responsible disposal of obsolete and discarded electronic and electrical equipment in accordance with applicable guidelines.

BIS Nagpur Celebrates World Standards Day 2026 with Focus on SDG 7: Affordable and Clean Energy
articles.full_content:
The Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS), Nagpur Branch Office, under the Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution, Government of India, celebrated World Standards Day 2026 at Nagpur, on 14 October 2026. The celebration focused on Sustainable Development Goal 7 (SDG 7): Affordable and Clean Energy, in line with this year’s theme, “Shared Vision for a Better World.”
Observed annually on 14 October, World Standards Day recognises the collaborative efforts of experts worldwide in developing voluntary consensus-based standards that facilitate technological advancement, promote quality and safety, and support sustainable development.
The programme commenced with a welcome address by Smt. Nisha Kanbargi, Joint Director, BIS Nagpur. Shri Raunak Sukhadeve, Joint Director, BIS Nagpur, subsequently presented messages from the International Organization for Standardization (ISO), the International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC) and the International Telecommunication Union (ITU), along with an overview of the significance of this year’s theme.
Dr. Manoj Kumar Rajak, Director and Head, BIS Nagpur Branch Office, outlined the objectives of the programme and highlighted the pivotal role of standardisation in bridging the gap between research and development (R&D) and industrial practices. He emphasised the need to strengthen quality infrastructure, address existing quality-related gaps, and develop Indian Standards that reflect the country’s climatic conditions, industrial requirements and practical applications.
Shri Ramchandra Ranganath Ukirde, Principal Director, National Power Training Institute (NPTI), the Chief Guest, provided insights into the prevailing energy scenario in India and globally. He discussed key challenges in the energy sector and outlined possible approaches to addressing them. He also underscored the importance of developing a skilled workforce, including trained technicians, engineers and IT professionals, to support the expansion of renewable energy. Highlighting NPTI’s initiatives, he spoke about its role in skill development, specialised training and placement opportunities for engineers in the power sector.
The inaugural session was followed by technical sessions featuring experts from leading academic and research institutions. Prof. Rajeev Agrawal, Professor of Practice in Production and Operations Management, Indian Institute of Management (IIM) Nagpur, discussed the role of effective project planning and management in achieving the Sustainable Development Goals, with particular emphasis on SDG 7 and the promotion of affordable and clean energy.
Shri Abhay Kumar Kuthe, Professor (HAG), Department of Mechanical Engineering, Visvesvaraya National Institute of Technology (VNIT), Nagpur, delivered a session on product innovation in the context of SDG 7 and its societal impact. Shri. Sivaguru Prabhakaran. IAS, District Collector, Ramanathapuram inaugurated new Aadhaar Seva Kendra
articles.full_content:
Unique Identification Authority of India (UIDAI) operationalized a new state-of-the art Aadhaar Seva Kendra (ASK) at Ramanathapuram, on Friday, 16th October 2026 marking another step towards strengthening resident-centric Aadhaar services in the district of Ramanathapuram.
The ASK Ramanathapuram was inaugurated by Thiru. M. Sivaguru Prabhakaran. IAS, District Collector of Ramanathapuram.
He appreciated the UIDAI’s effort and interacted with residents who visited ASK as well as the centre staff present there. Also, enquired about the Aadhaar enrolment and update procedures, and reviewed the various Aadhaar services being provided at the centre.
The ASK Ramanathapuram is equipped with 4 operational kits to provide seamless Aadhaar-related services to thousands of residents. The ASK is functional on all days except public holidays, thereby ensuring greater accessibility & convenience. The Aadhaar Seva Kendra offers Aadhaar enrolment, demographic and biometric updates, grievance redressal and other Aadhaar related services under one roof.
In addition to the enrolment and update transactions, ASK Ramanathapuram will also receive grievances from Aadhaar number holders for their resolution through the Regional Office.
With the inauguration of the Aadhaar Seva Kendra (ASK) at Ramanathapuram, UIDAI has now operationalised 24 Aadhaar Seva Kendras across Tamil Nadu. A further 06 ASKs are scheduled to become operational in the coming days across various districts, increasing the total 30 UIDAI-run Aadhaar Seva Kendras in the State.
The ASKs run by UIDAI, are designed to be fully inclusive and resident-friendly with facilities such as wheelchair accessibility, accessible restrooms, and a dedicated grievance redressal mechanism. Residents can also book appointments online for Aadhaar services at ASKs through UIDAI’s appointment portal: https://bookappointment.uidai.gov.in/ .
